description: Comparatorless charge-packet scouting probes each source through forward and reverse startup paths, ranks viable inputs, accumulates one minimum energy packet, then enables the main arbiter only once a safe handoff condition is latched.
mathematical_formalization: Choose source i maximizing ΔV_store/ΔQ_probe subject to I_backdrive_i <= I_limit and V_store >= V_handoff.
analogical_connections: speculative execution with commit only after validity
implementation_hypothesis: Use mirrored subthreshold pulse injectors plus capacitor slew comparison to estimate polarity/strength without an always-on comparator.

description: Maintain two startup reservoirs, one for forward-chargeable sources and one for reverse-suspect sources, and merge them only after a polarity-safe latch confirms that no source will be back-driven during handoff.

implementation_hypothesis: Use separate isolation FET stacks and tiny sign-detection packets to hold ambiguous sources out of the main startup bus until safe.
experiment_seed: Inject one positive and one inverted source with unequal source resistances and measure whether the architecture prevents wrong-way current while still reaching handoff.

description: Infer which weak source should be granted the first startup shot by comparing its response through two RC windows with different time constants, giving a coarse impedance classification without a powered comparator.
mathematical_formalization: rank_i = sgn((V_fast_i - V_slow_i)/(τ_fast - τ_slow)); choose argmax rank_i before arbitration enable.
implementation_hypothesis: A pair of passive time-constant sniffers plus dynamic sense switches can estimate whether a source is low-Z enough to survive a startup pulse.
experiment_seed: Hold source voltages equal and sweep impedance 1:1 to 1:20 to see whether the ranker chooses the source that actually minimizes startup delay and back-drive loss.
